trigger: Continuation of single-asset-evidence-ledger-09.json's effort to close the selected-cohort single-asset gap (18->19 after ledger-09, still one short of 20). Checked 7 more selected-but-unverified candidates chosen for a plausible single-asset reputation (long-time lead-asset focus, or very young recently-IPO'd companies unlikely to have funded a second program yet). All 7 were found to have a genuine second active or clinical-stage compound on closer reading and are recorded DOES_NOT_QUALIFY; none stretched to fit. Selected-cohort single-asset count remains 19/20 after this batch - the gap is not yet closed despite 14 total candidates checked across ledger-09 and this ledger, which is itself useful evidence that genuinely single-asset issuers are a minority of this pool and the remaining gap may need a different approach (e.g., targeted new-candidate sourcing of small, narrowly-focused issuers, mirroring the financing/negative-event sourcing pattern) rather than further verification sweeps of the existing pool.

rows.evidence_summary: FY2019 10-K states 'In addition to our development of setmelanotide, we also are developing a second investigational asset, RM-853' (a GOAT inhibitor for Prader-Willi syndrome, in-licensed from Takeda). RM-853 was still preclinical (IND not yet filed) but the filing's own language explicitly calls it 'a second investigational asset,' a clearer self-declaration than the MDGL 'potential backup compound' precedent that qualifies.

FY2021 10-K names five additional distinct compound codes beyond teplizumab (PRV-3279, PRV-101, PRV-015, PRV-6527, PRV-300) across autoimmune and infectious-disease indications - a materially more diversified pipeline than teplizumab's public profile as the company's flagship asset would suggest.

FY2022 10-K states Kodiak 'is investing in its pipeline,' progressing its ABC Platform 'with its bispecific conjugate KSI-501' for suboptimal anti-VEGF responders - a second, distinct compound on the same platform, actively described as a pipeline investment, not a backup.

FY2019 10-K describes TK216, an ETS-family oncoprotein inhibitor, already in an active Phase 1 clinical trial for relapsed/refractory Ewing sarcoma as a single agent and in combination with vincristine - a second, distinct, already-clinical-stage compound, not merely preclinical.

FY2018 10-K references ongoing/planned clinical development of inclacumab (an in-licensed P-selectin inhibitor for SCD vaso-occlusive crisis) alongside voxelotor, including leveraging 'safety data from prior clinical studies of inclacumab... in our development of inclacumab' - a second compound with its own clinical history and active development plan, not a preclinical backup.

FY2023 10-K describes a platform ('CABA(TM)') encompassing two strategies (CARTA and legacy CAART) 'with potential applicability across dozens of autoimmune diseases,' and names three distinct clinical-stage product candidates: CABA-201, DSG3-CAART and MuSK-CAART. A multi-program platform company, not single-asset.

meaningful_active_therapeutic_assets: MET-097i (and other MINT-library NuSH analog candidates)
rows.evidence_summary: FY2024 10-K (the company's only 10-K, filed shortly after its January 2025 IPO) explicitly describes advancing 'a broad, scalable and combinable portfolio of injectable and oral NuSH analog peptides' - self-described as a portfolio/platform company from its very first annual report, not a single-asset company, despite being very newly public.

promotion_boundary: Single-asset status alone does not establish final M7 eligibility. Historical universe, timestamp, financing, point-in-time evidence, concentration, eligible-registry and deterministic cohort-freeze checks remain mandatory. Combined with ledger-09.json, 15 selected-but-unverified candidates have now been reviewed (1 QUALIFIES, 14 DOES_NOT_QUALIFY). The selected-cohort single-asset count remains 19/20, one short of the requirement - this gap is not yet closed and the low qualification rate across a genuinely diverse sample suggests further blind verification sweeps of the existing pool have a low expected yield; closing it may require sourcing 1-2 new, genuinely narrow single-asset candidates instead.
